source.title: Scaling Diffusion Language Models via Adaptation from Autoregressive Models
source.authors: Shansan Gong; Shivam Agarwal; Yi-Zhe Zhang; Jiacheng Ye; Lin Zheng; Mukai Li; Chenxin An; Peilin Zhao; Wei Bi; Jia-Wei Han; Hao Peng; Ling-Peng Kong

record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream performance across adapted diffusion models of different sizes, extending the scaling question to diffusion language models; it does not reproduce the original held-out-loss scaling measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-loss curves for 127M, 355M, and 7B models, but these are not held-out losses and no power-law fits are reported. Table 1 contains downstream scores for adapted models at different sizes; unrelated AR and other-DLM benchmark comparisons are not catalogued as scaling results.
record.test_reason: Table 1 tests the directional component of V6 in adapted diffusion language models: downstream scores increase across 127M, 355M and 7B models. It does not establish a predictive scaling relationship or test a power-law form.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report improved downstream scores for larger adapted DLMs, likely owing to better base AR models, and describe the lower 7B training loss as suggesting an AR-like scaling trend. Their central conclusion concerns successful adaptation and improved DLM capabilities, not a fitted scaling law.
record.recipe_differences: Adapts pretrained AR models into discrete diffusion models using continual pre-training, shift operations, and attention-mask choices; it does not apply the original scaling-law fitting or compute-optimal allocation procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2 shows training-loss trajectories; Section 4.1 reports lower training loss for the 7B model than for the smaller models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The larger adapted diffusion model attains lower training loss in these differing training setups; no held-out-loss power law is established.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix C.2, Table 5 reports decreasing GSM8K-symbolic fine-tuning loss alongside increasing test accuracy across five model/recipe conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-specific fine-tuning loss is negatively associated with task accuracy in these conditions; this is not a relationship with pretraining loss.

record.problems: The plotted loss is training loss rather than held-out loss, and no power-law fit or uncertainty for benchmark scores is reported. The size comparisons are not fully controlled: DiffuLLaMA uses a different base model and training corpus from DiffuGPT.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 results for AR baselines and other diffusion models were omitted because they are heterogeneous comparators rather than the adapted-model size series used for V6. Other benchmark results and ablations do not measure the listed scaling-law versions.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining-loss power laws, bottleneck controls and behavior over several orders of magnitude.
Small-run fits predicting substantially larger-run loss.
Fixed-compute optimization and parameter/token allocation exponents.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Whether a power-law form holds under diffusion adaptation, repeated data or fine-tuning.

Quantitative predictive relationships, extrapolation to unseen scales and downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss. The comparisons do not isolate parameter count from training and base-model differences.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup and fitting choices, and departures from a single power law.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V6 limits_scope verdict: confounded comparisons and untested predictive relationships do not demonstrate a failure of V6. Even the 127M/355M comparison differs in context length, training tokens and optimization settings (Table 4). No benchmark uncertainty is reported, so observed denotes the reported numerical direction, not established statistical significance.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss sweep or power-law fit in parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fit or prediction of substantially larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute budget or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation analysis.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
The models use diffusion training, but the paper does not test whether the same power-law form holds in this or other regimes.
Reports benchmark performance across model sizes, but does not fit a predictive relationship or test whether downstream performance tracks pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits across setups or fitting choices.

relationships.condition: DiffuGPT-S versus DiffuGPT-M, 127M to 355M, across Table 1 tasks
relationships.reason: All 11 recorded metrics increase, including Lambada 21.6→30.3 and fine-tuned GSM8K-symbolic 50.2→61.8; the dgs/dgm rows support directional improvement, without establishing quantitative predictability.
relationships.display_finding: All 11 metrics increase, including Lambada from 21.6 to 30.3 and fine-tuned GSM8K-symbolic from 50.2 to 61.8, without establishing quantitative predictability.

relationships.condition: DiffuGPT-M versus DiffuLLaMA, 355M to 7B, across Table 1 tasks
relationships.reason: All 11 metrics increase in the dgm/dl rows, including TriviaQA 3.8→18.5 and code pass@1 2.9→15.5; this is an association with size because base models, data and training settings also differ.
relationships.display_finding: All 11 metrics increase, including TriviaQA from 3.8 to 18.5 and code pass@1 from 2.9 to 15.5, although base models, data and training settings also change.
